title: Cardiff University PhD Studentships and Projects 2026 | 100 Doctoral Opportunities
summary: Cardiff University is offering a wide range of PhD research studentships and projects across multiple academic disciplines for prospective doctoral researchers. The university s current PhD listings feature 100 doctoral opportunities , covering fields including Computer Science, Biological Sciences, Chemistry, Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, Medicine, Psychology, Environmental Sciences, Geography, Economics and more. The opportunities include directly funded and competition-funded research projects, with some positions open to students worldwide. Individual projects have different application deadlines, so applicants should carefully check the requirements and closing date for their selected project. About Cardiff University PhD Opportunities The available doctoral projects span a broad range of research areas and are hosted across Cardiff University s academic schools and research centres. The listings include opportunities in: Computer Science Biological Sciences Chemistry Engineering Physics and Astronomy Mathematics Medicine Psychology Healthcare Sciences Environmental Sciences Geography Economics Politics and Government Sociology Veterinary Sciences Materials Science Nursing and Health Communication and Media Studies Architecture, Building and Planning Languages, Literature and Culture The university s listing also includes specialised research groups such as Artificial Intelligence and Data Analytics, Biomedicine, Neuroscience, Molecular Biosciences, Cybersecurity, Privacy and HCC Research, and Organisms and Environment. Featured Cardiff University PhD Projects The current listing includes a variety of research projects across different schools. CyberInvent: Where Cybersecurity Research Meets Real-World Impact This PhD research project is hosted by the Cardiff School of Computer Science Informatics. The project is listed as directly funded and is open to UK students . Applications are accepted throughout the year. Mapping the Developing Brain This research project focuses on linking brain structure and function through imaging. It is hosted by the Cardiff School of Psychology and is listed as a competition-funded project open to students worldwide. Application deadline: 21 October 2026. Chronic Pain, Sensory Hypersensitivity and Neurodiversity This project investigates the relationship between chronic pain, sensory hypersensitivity and neurodiversity. The project is hosted by the Cardiff School of Psychology and is competition funded and open to students worldwide. Application deadline: 21 October 2026. Pain as Neurobiological Surprise This research project explores persistent pain using human brain imaging and animal studies. It is hosted by the Cardiff School of Psychology and is listed as competition funded and open to students worldwide. Application deadline: 21 October 2026. Search for Quantization of Space-Time with Photon Counting Interferometry This project is hosted by the Cardiff School of Physics and Astronomy. It is listed as a competition-funded PhD opportunity open to students worldwide. Application deadline: 30 October 2026. Adaptive Virtual-Reality Exergaming for Physical and Cognitive Health in Older Adults This research project is hosted by the Cardiff School of Healthcare Sciences. It is competition funded and open to students worldwide. Application deadline: 21 October 2026. Medication Adherence in Young People with First Episode Psychosis This project is a longitudinal mixed-methods biopsychosocial study examining decision-making and medication adherence among young people experiencing a first episode of psychosis. It is hosted by the Cardiff School of Healthcare Sciences and is listed as competition funded and open to students worldwide. Application deadline: 21 October 2026. Mapping Cerebellar Network Dysfunction in Episodic Ataxia This project is hosted by the Cardiff School of Biosciences and examines cerebellar network dysfunction using human organoids. It is listed as competition funded and open to students worldwide. Application deadline: 21 October 2026. From Multi-OMICs to Mechanism This Cardiff School of Biosciences project focuses on understanding links between protein turnover and therapy resistance in glioblastoma stem cells. It is listed as competition funded and open to students worldwide. Application deadline: 21 October 2026. Gene-Diet Interaction and Psychiatric Risk This project investigates gene-diet interactions and psychiatric risk, with a focus on FADS2 and dietary polyunsaturated fatty acids. It is hosted by the Cardiff School of Biosciences and is competition funded and open to students worldwide. Application deadline: 21 October 2026. Funding Opportunities The Cardiff University listing distinguishes between different funding statuses. The current search page includes categories for: UK students European students excluding the UK Non-European students Self-funded students Applicants should therefore check the funding status attached to each individual PhD project rather than assuming that every listed doctoral opportunity carries the same funding arrangement. The current first page also identifies some projects as directly funded and others as competition funded . Application Deadlines There is no single deadline covering all the listed PhD projects. For example, the current listings show: CyberInvent — applications accepted all year round Several Psychology, Healthcare Sciences and Biosciences projects — 21 October 2026 Photon-counting interferometry project — 30 October 2026 Applicants should therefore review the individual project page for the latest deadline, eligibility conditions and application procedure. How to Find a Suitable PhD Project Prospective applicants can use the Cardiff University PhD studentships and projects listing to search according to several criteria. The listing provides filters for: Department Supervisor Discipline Research Group Funding Status Keywords This allows prospective students to narrow the available projects according to their academic interests, preferred supervisor, research field and funding circumstances. Research Supervisors The current Cardiff University listing includes a large number of potential PhD supervisors across different schools and disciplines. The supervisor filter includes academics such as Dr Nitesh Kumar, Dr Mohammad Al-Amri, Prof Pete Burnap, Prof Mara Cercignani, Prof H. Grote, Prof P. Sumner, Dr George Tackley, Dr Yasir Syed and many others. Applicants should examine the research interests of the supervisor attached to their selected project before applying. Why Applicants Should Check Individual Projects The 100 available projects do not all have identical funding arrangements, deadlines or eligibility requirements. For example, the CyberInvent project is directly funded and accepts applications throughout the year, while several other projects are competition funded and have specific October 2026 deadlines. Applicants should therefore avoid treating the entire listing as one single scholarship programme. Instead, they should select a specific research project and review its individual requirements before submitting an application. Application Portal: Cardiff University PHD Studentships Conclusion Cardiff University s current PhD studentships and projects listing provides prospective doctoral researchers with access to 100 PhD opportunities across a broad range of academic disciplines. The opportunities cover areas from artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, engineering and physics to healthcare, psychology, biosciences, environmental sciences and other social and scientific disciplines. Some projects are directly funded, while others are competition funded, and eligibility varies between projects. Several current opportunities are open to students worldwide, while others have more specific funding eligibility. Interested applicants should use the university s search filters to identify suitable projects, examine the funding status and deadline of their chosen opportunity, review the supervisor and research topic, and then follow the application instructions for that specific project. title: French Republic Human Rights Prize 2026 | €70,000 Grant for Human Rights Projects
summary: Applications are now open for the 2026 French Republic Human Rights Prize “Liberty – Equality – Fraternity” , an international human rights award established in 1988 to recognise and support individual or collective grassroots initiatives that contribute to the promotion and protection of human rights. The prize, awarded by the Prime Minister of the French Government, is open to individual applicants and non-governmental organisations regardless of nationality or borders . For the 2026 edition, applicants are invited to submit projects focused on protecting the right to asylum and the fundamental rights of refugees, asylum seekers and displaced persons . Five winning projects will share a total grant of €70,000 to support the implementation of their projects. The five winners will also be invited to Paris to attend the official award ceremony and will receive a medal. The application deadline is 4 October 2026 at midnight (GMT+1) . About the French Republic Human Rights Prize The French Republic Human Rights Prize “Liberty – Equality – Fraternity” was established in 1988. The prize is intended to recognise and support grassroots initiatives carried out in France or abroad that contribute to the promotion or protection of human rights. Applications may be submitted by individuals or organisations, and applicants are not required to be French nationals. The award is administered through the National Consultative Commission on Human Rights (CNCDH) . 2026 Prize Theme The single theme for the 2026 edition is: Protecting the Right to Asylum and the Fundamental Rights of Refugees, Asylum Seekers and Displaced Persons Applicants must submit an action or project that addresses this theme and is intended to be implemented in France or another country. The 2026 theme focuses on protecting the right to asylum and ensuring that people affected by forced displacement can effectively access their fundamental rights. Background to the 2026 Theme The right to asylum provides protection to people who are unable to rely on the protection of their own country. The right is recognised under international refugee law, including the 1951 Geneva Convention relating to the Status of Refugees and its 1967 Protocol . The call for applications also refers to Article 14 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights , which recognises the right to seek and enjoy asylum from persecution. The 2026 call highlights the importance of strengthening legal systems that protect the right to asylum and incorporate international human rights and refugee law into domestic legislation. The call also notes the scale of forced displacement around the world. According to figures cited in the call from the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), there were 117.3 million forcibly displaced people worldwide at the end of June 2025 , including recognised refugees, asylum seekers and internally displaced people. Who Can Submit an Application? Applications can be submitted by: Individuals Non-governmental organisations Organisations implementing human-rights-based projects Applicants of any nationality The applicant must have a project or action related to guaranteeing the right to asylum and protecting the fundamental rights of people experiencing forced displacement. Projects may concern refugees covered by the Geneva Convention, asylum seekers whose applications are being examined, or people displaced within their own countries. What Types of Projects Are Eligible? The prize is intended for projects based on a human-rights approach that seek to guarantee the right to asylum and fundamental rights. Particular consideration will be given to projects that: Provide comprehensive support to affected individuals Implement transformative and restorative measures Ensure the active participation of people directly concerned by the project The projects should focus on rights protection, advocacy, legal support or related activities rather than direct material assistance. Examples of Eligible Projects The 2026 call identifies several types of projects that may be considered. Public Awareness and Advocacy Projects may raise public awareness about asylum and refugee rights or undertake advocacy directed at public authorities. Such initiatives could seek to improve understanding of legal protections and promote policies or practices that protect the rights of displaced people. Legal and Administrative Assistance Projects may provide legal and administrative assistance to refugees, asylum seekers and internally displaced persons. This may include helping people effectively access rights such as: Residence rights Fair procedures Access to justice Civil and political rights Economic rights Social rights Cultural rights Projects should be connected to rights guaranteed under applicable international instruments. Training for Stakeholders Eligible initiatives may provide training to stakeholders involved in asylum and displacement matters. Potential participants may include: Border police Government administrations Health services Social services Other professionals involved in asylum procedures The objective can be to strengthen understanding and implementation of human rights obligations. Integration, Resettlement and Restoration of Rights Projects may support the effective exercise of rights associated with integration into host societies. They may also address resettlement or the restoration of rights for internally displaced people. Prize and Financial Award Five projects will be selected as winners. The five winners will share a total grant of: €70,000 The grant is allocated by the National Consultative Commission on Human Rights (CNCDH) for implementation of the winning projects. The five winners will also receive a medal and may refer to themselves as laureates of the 2026 French Republic Human Rights Prize . Special Mentions In addition to the five winners, the next five highest-ranked candidates will receive a Special Mention medal . The Special Mention is awarded by the Ambassador of France in the recipient s country of origin. Special Mention recipients do not receive a financial award. Prize winners and Special Mention recipients may also benefit from international protection afforded by French diplomacy. Award Ceremony The five prize winners will be invited to Paris, France , to attend the official award ceremony. The 2026 Prize is expected to be formally awarded around 10 December 2026 , which is International Human Rights Day. The award will be presented by the Prime Minister or another Minister of the French Republic. Application Requirements Applicants must submit a complete application file. The application must include the following: 1. Letter of Application Applicants must provide a signed letter of application. For an NGO, the letter must be submitted and signed by the organisation s President or legal representative. Individual applicants must submit and sign their own application letter. 2. Completed Application Form Applicants must complete the official application form provided with the call for applications. The form provides detailed information about the activities carried out by the applicant or organisation. The application form is available through the CNCDH website. 3. Postal and Banking Details Applicants must provide their postal and banking information. This includes the relevant RIB/IBAN details of the NGO or individual applicant. Language of the Application The application file should be drafted in French . However, the call states that applications submitted in English or Spanish may be considered at the discretion of the jury . Applicants who can submit their application in French should follow the stated language requirement. Application Deadline The complete application must be submitted no later than: 4 October 2026 at midnight (GMT+1) Applications received after the deadline may not be considered. Applicants should therefore allow sufficient time to complete the application form, prepare supporting information and submit the complete application file. How to Apply Applicants should: Review the 2026 French Republic Human Rights Prize theme. Confirm that their project addresses the protection of asylum rights and the fundamental rights of refugees, asylum seekers or displaced persons. Review the official Prize Rules. Download and complete the official application form. Prepare the required signed application letter. Prepare the applicant s postal and banking details, including RIB/IBAN. Prepare the application in French, where possible. Submit the complete application before the deadline. Applications can be submitted by post or email. Postal Submission CNCDH – For the attention of Mrs. Cécile RIOU-BATISTA 20 avenue de Ségur 75007 Paris France Email Submission prixdesdroitsdelhomme@cncdh.fr Important Application Information Applicants should carefully review the official Prize Rules before submitting their applications. The official rules and application information are available through the CNCDH website. Applicants should also ensure that their proposed project is clearly connected to the 2026 theme and focuses on human rights protection rather than direct material assistance. Conclusion The 2026 French Republic Human Rights Prize “Liberty – Equality – Fraternity” provides an opportunity for individuals and NGOs to gain recognition and financial support for projects protecting the rights of refugees, asylum seekers and displaced persons. The 2026 edition focuses specifically on protecting the right to asylum and the fundamental rights of refugees, asylum seekers and displaced persons . Five selected winners will share €70,000 for the implementation of their projects and will be invited to Paris for the official award ceremony. Five additional candidates will receive Special Mention medals without a financial award. Eligible applicants should prepare their project information, application letter, official application form and required banking and postal details before submitting their complete application. The application deadline is 4 October 2026 at midnight (GMT+1) . Discover more opportunities on the OFY Webpage . title: Fulcrum Fellowship 2026 | Leadership Fellowship for Community Investment Leaders
summary: The Fulcrum Fellowship 2026 is now accepting applications for a 13-month leadership development programme designed for experienced leaders working to strengthen community investment, capital, policy and practice. Organised by the Center for Community Investment (CCI), the fellowship supports leaders who are already engaged in strategic work that can help build more just and resilient communities, with particular attention to small- and mid-size cities and communities across the South. The programme combines collaborative problem-solving, personalised coaching, systems thinking, peer learning and in-person seminars to help fellows strengthen their leadership practice and develop actionable strategies for their communities. Applications close on October 15, 2026. About the Fulcrum Fellowship The Fulcrum Fellowship is designed for established leaders who have significant responsibility within their organisations and are working on challenges where access to capital can contribute to community-level change. Over the course of 13 months, fellows will participate in a combination of in-person and virtual activities designed to strengthen their ability to develop strategies, collaborate across sectors and use capital more effectively. The programme creates a cohort of leaders with diverse experiences, sectors, geographies and career paths. What the Fellowship Offers Throughout the 13-month programme, fellows participate in: Collaborative problem-solving Personalised leadership coaching Systems-thinking exercises Five multi-day in-person seminars Monthly virtual coaching sessions Group learning sessions Peer networking Leadership development Strategies for community investment and capital deployment The programme is designed to connect fellows with peers who are addressing complementary challenges in different communities and sectors. CCI s Capital Absorption Framework A central component of the Fulcrum Fellowship is the Center for Community Investment s Capital Absorption Framework. Fellows use the framework and related systems-thinking tools to better understand how capital moves through communities and how different structures influence the ability of communities to access and use capital. Through this work, fellows develop strategies for advancing community-defined priorities and addressing systemic barriers that affect opportunity. In-Person Seminars Applicants should be prepared to participate in five in-person seminars in Berkeley, California . The scheduled seminar dates are: April 13–15, 2027 July 13–15, 2027 October 26–28, 2027 February 1–3, 2028 May 2–4, 2028 Participation in these sessions is part of the 13-month fellowship commitment. Experienced Faculty and Peer Learning The fellowship is led by experienced faculty and brings together a diverse group of leaders working on community investment and related challenges. The cohort-based structure gives participants opportunities to learn from other leaders, exchange experiences and test new approaches to leadership and capital strategy. Fellows can also develop relationships with peers who may continue collaborating beyond the programme. What Fellows Gain The Fulcrum Fellowship is designed to help participants strengthen their ability to: Move capital toward community-defined priorities Apply systems-thinking approaches to complex challenges Develop stronger leadership strategies Reconsider existing approaches to community investment Work collaboratively across sectors Build relationships with other leaders Strengthen organisational capacity Develop practical strategies for community-level change Fellows also become part of a network of leaders working to influence the broader community investment ecosystem. What Organisations Gain The benefits of the programme extend beyond individual fellows. Participants can bring new leadership approaches, strategies and relationships back to their organisations. The programme is intended to help fellows develop sharper strategies, stronger networks and leadership tools that can be applied to their organisations and communities. Who Can Apply? The Fulcrum Fellowship is designed for experienced leaders with meaningful authority within their organisations and a strong network of colleagues and partners with whom they can work. Applicants should demonstrate experience and an established commitment to community-focused work. Eligible applicants should: Lead Strategic Work Applicants should be leading strategic work that has meaningful importance to their organisation, community or broader field. Demonstrate a Commitment to Racial Equity Applicants should be committed to advancing racial equity and be able to demonstrate tangible results or sustained efforts through their work. Have Significant Professional Experience Applicants should have 10 to 15 years of experience working in one of the programme s focus fields. These include: Shared ownership Climate resilience Housing and community development Creative placemaking Philanthropy Finance Be Willing to Rethink Existing Strategies Fellows should be open to reconsidering and reframing existing strategies in order to accelerate progress and deepen their impact. Develop Leadership Self-Awareness Applicants should be interested in developing greater self-awareness and personal effectiveness as leaders. Participate in Coaching and Peer Learning Successful fellows should be willing to learn, give and receive coaching and actively participate in a network of diverse peers. Commit to the Full Programme Applicants must be able to commit to the entire 13-month programme . The application also requires written endorsement from the applicant s organisation. Information Session CCI will host an information session for prospective applicants. Date: September 28, 2026 Time: 1:00 p.m. CT / 2:00 p.m. ET The session will feature Fulcrum alum and CCI Executive Director Omar Carrillo Tinajero . Interested applicants can attend to learn more about the fellowship and hear directly from programme leadership and alumni. Application Deadline The Fulcrum Fellowship 2026 application deadline is: October 15, 2026 Applicants are encouraged to review the programme requirements and application materials carefully before submitting their applications. How to Apply Interested applicants should: Review the Fulcrum Fellowship programme criteria. Confirm that their professional experience aligns with the fellowship requirements. Review the application guide and frequently asked questions. Discuss the fellowship commitment with their organisation. Obtain the required organisational endorsement. Prepare the application materials. Submit the application before October 15, 2026 . Conclusion The Fulcrum Fellowship 2026 provides an intensive 13-month leadership development experience for experienced community investment leaders working across areas such as housing and community development, climate resilience, finance, philanthropy, shared ownership and creative placemaking. Through coaching, peer learning, systems thinking and five in-person seminars in Berkeley, California, fellows will have opportunities to strengthen their leadership practice and develop strategies for moving capital toward community-defined priorities. The fellowship is intended for established leaders with significant professional experience, organisational responsibility and a demonstrated commitment to advancing racial equity and community-level change. Interested applicants should review the eligibility criteria and prepare their applications before the October 15, 2026 deadline . Discover more on the OFY Webpage . title: CGBD Research Fellowship 2026–2027: Apply for DIFFvelopment’s Global Black Community Research Fellowship
summary: \The CGBD Research Fellowship by DIFFvelopment offers undergraduate students, graduate students and visionary thinkers from around the world an opportunity to develop research ideas focused on the future and sustainable empowerment of Black communities globally. The fellowship is designed for emerging researchers and thinkers who want to move beyond conventional approaches and develop bold, solutions-driven research that can contribute to meaningful change across Black communities. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis , with applications submitted by 31 July each year considered for the upcoming fellowship cycle beginning in November. Applications submitted after 31 July will generally be considered for the following fellowship cycle. About the CGBD Research Fellowship The CGBD Fellowship is a research-focused initiative run by DIFFvelopment . According to the programme overview provided, the fellowship seeks to empower young researchers to reimagine the future of the global Black community through bold, solutions-driven research . Rather than simply focusing on academic research for its own sake, the programme invites participants to develop actionable research plans that can contribute to sustainable empowerment across Black communities globally. This makes the fellowship relevant to individuals interested in using research, ideas and evidence to explore challenges and opportunities affecting Black communities. What Is the Purpose of the Fellowship? The CGBD Research Fellowship is centred on the development of research that can contribute to the long-term empowerment of Black communities. Participants are expected to think critically about issues affecting Black communities and develop research plans that can potentially contribute to solutions. The programme s stated focus includes: Reimagining the future of the global Black community. Developing bold and solutions-driven research. Creating actionable research plans. Supporting sustainable empowerment. Encouraging young researchers and visionary thinkers. Connecting research with issues affecting Black communities globally. The emphasis on actionable research means applicants should consider not only what problem they want to study, but also how their research can contribute to practical understanding, solutions or positive change. APPLY HERE Who Is Invited to Apply? The programme specifically invites: Undergraduate students Graduate students Visionary thinkers The opportunity is open to applicants worldwide , according to the programme overview supplied. This broad eligibility makes the fellowship relevant to people at different stages of their academic and research journeys, as well as thinkers who may have ideas that extend beyond a traditional academic pathway. What Will Selected Fellows Do? Selected participants will develop actionable research plans . This means fellows will be expected to take their research interests or ideas and develop them into structured plans that address issues relevant to sustainable empowerment across Black communities. The fellowship therefore provides an opportunity to develop research thinking around questions such as: What challenges are affecting Black communities? What evidence is needed to better understand those challenges? What solutions could potentially address identified issues? How can research contribute to sustainable empowerment? How can research findings eventually be translated into practical action? Applicants should therefore consider how their proposed research can go beyond identifying a problem and contribute toward understanding possible solutions. A Global Focus on Black Communities One of the defining characteristics of the CGBD Fellowship is its global perspective . The programme refers to the global Black community , rather than restricting its focus to one country or region. This creates room for research examining issues affecting Black communities in different geographical contexts. Depending on the researcher s interests, potential areas of inquiry could include issues affecting Black communities across different countries and regions, provided the proposed research aligns with the programme s stated focus on sustainable empowerment. The global orientation can also provide an opportunity for applicants to think about similarities and differences between Black communities in different parts of the world. Solutions-Driven Research The fellowship places particular emphasis on solutions-driven research . Solutions-driven research focuses not only on understanding a problem but also on exploring practical approaches that could help address it. For applicants, this means a strong research concept should clearly communicate: The issue being investigated. Why the issue matters. The community or communities affected. The research questions being considered. What the research aims to discover. How the findings could contribute to solutions. How the research could support sustainable empowerment. Applicants should therefore approach their proposals with both research and potential impact in mind. Developing an Actionable Research Plan A central component of the fellowship is the development of an actionable research plan . An actionable plan provides a structured pathway for turning an idea into research that can realistically be pursued. Applicants should think carefully about the relationship between their research problem, objectives and expected outcomes. A well-developed research concept can help demonstrate that the applicant has thought about how their proposed work could contribute to the broader objectives of the CGBD Fellowship. Who May Benefit From the Opportunity? The fellowship can be relevant to students and thinkers interested in a wide range of issues connected to Black communities. Potential applicants may include people working or studying in areas where research can contribute to community empowerment, social development, education, economics, policy, culture, technology, health, entrepreneurship or other fields. However, the supplied programme overview does not provide a definitive list of eligible research disciplines. Applicants should therefore consult the full CGBD Fellowship Overview for the programme s detailed research requirements. Fellowship Funding and Financial Support The CGBD Fellowship is explicitly described as an unpaid opportunity . Applicants should therefore understand that participation does not constitute paid employment and that the programme does not provide a standard fellowship salary based on the information supplied. However, DIFFvelopment states that fellows who demonstrate financial need may be eligible for a modest technology stipend . The purpose of this stipend is to support: Internet access Remote participation Technology-related needs associated with participating in the fellowship The availability of this support is subject to eligibility and demonstrated financial need. Applicants should not assume that every fellow will automatically receive the technology stipend. Is the CGBD Fellowship a Paid Opportunity? No. The programme overview specifically states that the CGBD Fellowship is unpaid . However, fellows who demonstrate financial need may be considered for a modest technology stipend to assist with internet access and remote participation. Therefore, applicants should distinguish between the fellowship itself and the possible technology support. Application Timeline The CGBD Fellowship follows a rolling application process . This means applications are not limited to one fixed application period during the year. However, there is an important annual consideration date: Applications submitted by 31 July Applications received by 31 July each year will be considered for the upcoming CGBD Fellowship cycle beginning in November . Applications submitted after 31 July Applications submitted after 31 July will generally be considered for the following fellowship cycle . This distinction is important for applicants planning when to submit their applications. For example, an applicant submitting before the annual 31 July consideration date may be considered for the cycle beginning in November, while an application submitted after that date will generally move into consideration for the subsequent cycle. Application Deadline The programme operates on a rolling basis rather than having one permanent annual closing date. The key annual date stated in the programme information is: 31 July each year — applications submitted by this date are considered for the upcoming fellowship cycle beginning in November. Applications submitted after 31 July will generally be considered for the following cycle. Because the programme operates on this rolling basis, applicants should review the current application information before submitting to confirm which fellowship cycle their application will be considered for. Visit HERE to learn more about the CGBD Research Fellowship 2026–2027 How to Apply Applicants interested in the CGBD Research Fellowship should review the programme s full fellowship overview before applying. The supplied programme information provides a CGBD Fellowship Overview containing the full programme details: CGBD Fellowship Overview The full overview should be consulted for detailed information about the application requirements, research expectations and fellowship process that are not included in the short programme summary provided. Important Note for Applicants DIFFvelopment states that it does not engage external recruiters or agencies . Applicants should therefore be cautious about anyone claiming to represent DIFFvelopment as an external recruiter or agency in connection with the CGBD Fellowship. Applicants should use the official programme information and application process when seeking to participate. Key Details at a Glance Detail Information Programme CGBD Research Fellowship Organisation DIFFvelopment Focus Solutions-driven research and sustainable empowerment across Black communities globally Eligible applicants Undergraduate students, graduate students and visionary thinkers Geographic scope Worldwide Compensation Unpaid Possible support Modest technology stipend for fellows demonstrating financial need Application system Rolling basis Annual consideration date 31 July Upcoming cycle Beginning in November After 31 July Generally considered for the following cycle Why Applicants Should Consider the Fellowship The CGBD Fellowship provides an opportunity for participants to develop research ideas around issues affecting Black communities globally. For students, it can provide an avenue for turning academic interests into a more structured research plan. For visionary thinkers, it creates an opportunity to explore ideas through a research-oriented framework focused on sustainable empowerment. The programme s emphasis on solutions-driven research also encourages participants to think about how research can contribute to practical change rather than simply describing existing challenges. What Applicants Should Pay Attention To Before applying, prospective fellows should carefully consider whether their proposed research aligns with the core focus of the programme. In particular, applicants should consider: Relevance: Is the proposed research connected to the future and empowerment of Black communities? Research focus: Is there a clear issue or question that the research will investigate? Solutions: Does the proposed work explore potential solutions or actionable outcomes? Impact: Could the research contribute to sustainable empowerment? Feasibility: Can the proposed research realistically be developed and carried out? Programme requirements: Does the application meet the requirements contained in the full CGBD Fellowship Overview? Applicants should use the full programme documentation to confirm any detailed requirements that are not included in the summary. Conclusion The CGBD Research Fellowship by DIFFvelopment is a global research opportunity designed for undergraduate students, graduate students and visionary thinkers interested in developing bold, solutions-driven research focused on the future and sustainable empowerment of Black communities. The programme provides selected participants with an opportunity to develop actionable research plans and explore ideas that can contribute to meaningful understanding and potential solutions affecting Black communities globally. The fellowship is unpaid , although fellows who demonstrate financial need may be eligible for a modest technology stipend to assist with internet access and remote participation. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis . Applications submitted by 31 July each year are considered for the upcoming fellowship cycle beginning in November, while applications submitted after 31 July will generally be considered for the following cycle. Prospective applicants should review the full CGBD Fellowship Overview carefully before submitting an application and should rely on DIFFvelopment s official programme information for the latest requirements and application instructions. title: Research Fellow (West Africa) at Chatham House: Full-Time Policy Research Job in London
summary: The Chatham House Africa Programme is inviting applications for a Research Fellow (West Africa) to contribute to independent policy research and convening activities focused on West Africa, with significant work on Nigeria and scope to expand regional coverage over time. This is a full-time, permanent position based in London , offering an annual salary of £45,000 . The successful candidate will join Chatham House’s Africa Programme and contribute to research covering governance, politics, economy and trade, security, and the wider regional and international relationships of African states. The application deadline is Tuesday, 29 September 2026 at 23:59 BST . About the Chatham House Africa Programme The Africa Programme conducts policy research examining issues affecting individual African states as well as their regional and international relations. The programme seeks to produce research that is relevant to policymakers and contributes to discussions on major political, economic, governance and security issues affecting the continent. As a Research Fellow, the successful applicant will contribute to this work through research projects, publications, stakeholder engagement, events and conferences. The position is particularly focused on West Africa , including substantial work on Nigeria , while also providing an opportunity for the researcher to expand their regional coverage over time. The role therefore combines academic and policy-oriented research with practical engagement with stakeholders and the wider policy community. Research Fellow (West Africa) Role Overview The Research Fellow will be expected to contribute to the development and delivery of a range of research and convening activities relating to West Africa. The position covers several major thematic areas, including: Politics and governance Economy and trade Security Regional affairs International relations Policy research and analysis The successful candidate will also contribute to significant research work concerning Nigeria and will have the opportunity to work across different issues affecting West Africa. This makes the position suitable for an experienced researcher who can work across multiple policy areas rather than focusing exclusively on one narrow research topic. Key Responsibilities 1. Designing and Delivering Research Projects A major responsibility of the Research Fellow will be to help develop and deliver research projects that support the strategic objectives of the Africa Programme and Chatham House. This includes contributing to research from the initial development stage through to the production and dissemination of findings. The successful candidate will therefore need to be capable of identifying important research questions, developing research proposals and contributing to projects that have clear policy relevance. Research projects will be expected to advance understanding of important developments in West Africa and generate findings that can contribute to policy discussions. 2. Producing Policy-Relevant Research The Research Fellow will produce high-quality research relating to West Africa. The position specifically covers research across areas such as: Politics Governance Economy Trade Security The role requires more than simply producing academic research. The research should be policy relevant , meaning that the findings should be useful to people involved in understanding, developing or implementing policy. The researcher will therefore need to demonstrate the ability to analyse complex issues, identify important developments and communicate findings clearly to a policy audience. 3. Research on Nigeria and West Africa The role includes significant work on Nigeria , alongside broader research covering West Africa. Nigeria is one of the major areas of focus mentioned in the position, meaning applicants should be prepared to engage deeply with developments affecting the country while also understanding the wider regional context. The position also provides scope for the successful researcher to expand their regional coverage over time . This means the role can involve developing expertise beyond an initial area of specialization as the researcher contributes to the broader work of the Africa Programme. 4. Developing Research Proposals The successful candidate will be expected to have experience developing successful research proposals. title: AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grants 2026: Up to €3,000 for Doctoral Researchers in Sub-Saharan Africa
summary: The AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grants for Junior Researchers 2026 are now open to eligible doctoral researchers from sub-Saharan Africa seeking financial support to undertake a short research stay at a university or research institute in another sub-Saharan African country. Supported by the German Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation (AvH) , the programme is designed to strengthen scientific capacity, research collaboration, networking, and knowledge exchange among young researchers across sub-Saharan Africa. The grants enable eligible doctoral candidates to spend one to two months at a host university or research institution in another sub-Saharan African country while working with an experienced scientific host. The research stay must contribute directly to the applicant s doctoral research. For the 2026 call, applications must be submitted in English by 16 October 2026 at 23:59 GMT . What Are the AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grants? The AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grants are research mobility opportunities designed to support junior researchers pursuing doctoral degrees in sub-Saharan Africa . The programme allows doctoral candidates to temporarily move to another sub-Saharan African country to undertake research activities that cannot be conducted in their home country. During the research stay, the researcher works with an identified scientific host at a university or research institute. The programme aims to strengthen: Scientific research capacity Research collaboration between African institutions Professional networks among young researchers International scientific networking Knowledge and skills transfer Collaboration between doctoral researchers and experienced researchers Research that contributes to the development of sub-Saharan African countries The programme is supported financially by BMZ and with support from the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation . Two AGNES Mobility Grant Programmes The 2026 call provides two different mobility grant opportunities. 1. General AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grant The General AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grant is generally open to both male and female candidates . Eligible male and female doctoral researchers can apply for this grant provided they meet the programme requirements. 2. Special AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grant The Special AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grant is specifically for female candidates . Female researchers may apply for either the General Grant, the Special Grant, or both. However, a female applicant can receive a maximum of one grant . Male candidates are only eligible to apply for the General AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grant. AGNES also encourages applications from researchers across a wide range of disciplines, including: Sciences Humanities Law Social Sciences No Geographical Quota The 2026 call states that there is no geographical quota for AGNES grants within sub-Saharan Africa. This means eligible candidates from sub-Saharan African countries can apply. However, AGNES specifically welcomes applications from eligible candidates from countries described in the call as under-represented. These include: Burkina Faso Ghana Guinea Côte d’Ivoire Liberia Mali Senegal Sierra Leone Angola Central African Republic Chad Congo Brazzaville Democratic Republic of the Congo Equatorial Guinea Gabon Rwanda Zambia Uganda Tanzania Malawi Lesotho Botswana Mozambique Mauritius Mauritania Namibia Zimbabwe Cape Verde Sao Tome and Principe Importantly, being from one of these countries is not presented as an exclusive eligibility requirement . The call states that all eligible candidates from sub-Saharan African countries can apply. What Does the Grant Support? The AGNES Mobility Grant enables a doctoral researcher to undertake a research stay lasting between one and two months at a university or research institute in another sub-Saharan African country. The proposed research must form part of the applicant s doctoral research. Eligible activities may include: Laboratory research Bench work Research studies Library research Data or other research activities Writing part of the doctoral thesis Other activities directly related to the doctoral research The proposed research should contribute meaningfully to the applicant s doctoral work. The applicant must also demonstrate why the research is relevant to the further development of their home country or other sub-Saharan African countries. Research Must Not Be Possible in the Home Country One of the important conditions is that the proposed research activity cannot be conducted in the applicant s home country . Applicants therefore need to demonstrate why the host institution provides research facilities, expertise, resources, or other conditions that are unavailable in the applicant s home country. This is an important consideration when preparing the research proposal. Financial Support The AGNES grant is intended to be financially comprehensive for the short research stay as far as reasonably possible. The grant can support expenses associated with: Travel Subsistence Research-related expenses Host institution research costs, where applicable The maximum grant depends on the length of the research stay. Maximum Grant Amounts Research Stay Maximum Grant 1 month €2,300 1.5 months €2,650 2 months €3,000 These amounts represent the maximum overall budget, including the host fee. Research Allowance for the Host Institution A portion of the grant may be allocated to research costs at the host institution. The call specifies the following deductions from the total grant: Humanities and Social Sciences: €100 per month Natural and Life Sciences and Engineering Sciences: €200 per month The scientific host and host institution must request the relevant research cost allowance as part of the required documentation. Travel Support Applicants must provide two travel quotations for their journey. The quotes should cover return travel between: The applicant s country of residence; and The country where the host institution is located. Travel may be by: Land transportation; or Economy-class flight Applicants should therefore research the expected cost of their return journey before submitting the application. Cost of Living Applicants must also provide an estimate of their expected cost of living during the research stay. This should take into account expenses such as: Accommodation or rent Meals Local transportation Health insurance Applicants are expected to obtain valid health insurance for the duration of their research stay. The scientific host and host institution are expected to assist applicants in finding affordable accommodation and preparing realistic subsistence estimates. APPLY HERE Who Can Apply? The programme is specifically aimed at junior researchers who are currently pursuing doctoral degrees in sub-Saharan Africa. Applicants must meet several eligibility requirements. 1. Must Be a Doctoral Student The applicant must be officially registered for a doctoral degree at a university or tertiary institution in sub-Saharan Africa at the time of application. Current doctoral students are eligible. The call specifically states that applicants must provide official proof of registration for their postgraduate degree. 2. Must Be a National of a Sub-Saharan African Country Applicants must be nationals of a sub-Saharan African country . The programme therefore focuses specifically on researchers from sub-Saharan Africa. 3. Must Have at Least One Published Research Article Applicants must have at least one published article from their thesis work . The article must have been published in a non-predatory journal . The call specifies that only journals indexed by: SCOPUS , or Web of Science will be considered. Applicants therefore need to provide evidence that their publication meets these requirements. 4. Research Must Be Relevant to Development The applicant must clearly demonstrate how their research contributes to the development of sub-Saharan African countries. The proposal should therefore explain the broader relevance and potential development contribution of the research. 5. Research Must Require the Host Institution The applicant must demonstrate that the proposed research cannot be conducted in their home country . This requirement helps ensure that the mobility component of the grant is necessary for the proposed research. 6. Identified Scientific Host Required Applicants must already have an identified scientific host . The applicant and scientific host must agree on: The research proposal The research activities The work schedule The timing of the research stay Applications without an identified scientific host and mutually agreed proposal/work schedule will not be considered. Required Application Documents Applicants must submit a complete application containing all required documents. The maximum total application size is 12 MB . 1. Research or Project Proposal Applicants must prepare a short research/project proposal. The proposal: Must be written in English. Must not exceed five pages. Must outline the proposed research activity. Must explain the research objectives. Must include a work schedule. Must explain how the research will be undertaken at the host institution. The scientific host must agree in writing to the proposal and proposed schedule. 2. Standard CV Applicants must submit a standard CV using the AGNES CV template . The CV must be written in English. The official 2026 AGNES Mobility CV template is provided as part of the application information. 3. Proof of Doctoral Registration Applicants must provide official proof that they are currently registered for their doctoral degree. This is an important requirement because the programme is specifically intended for current doctoral students. 4. Academic Transcripts Applicants must submit official academic transcripts showing grades obtained during: Undergraduate studies Postgraduate studies, where applicable If the transcript is written in a language other than English, applicants must also provide an official explanation of the grading system in English . 5. List of Publications Applicants must provide a list of their published articles in eligible non-predatory journals. The publication list must include SCOPUS or Web of Science links for each publication. Applicants must also include an electronic copy of the first page of each publication showing: Article title Authors Abstract The publication list and first pages of the publications must be combined into one PDF document . The document should begin with a descriptive title, such as: “LIST OF PUBLICATIONS FOR [APPLICANT S NAME]” The publication list should then be followed by the first page of each publication. 6. Travel Quotations Applicants must provide two travel quotations for return travel between their country of residence and the host institution s country. The quotes can cover: Land travel; or Economy-class air travel 7. Estimated Cost of Living Applicants must provide an estimated budget for their stay. The estimate should cover: Rent/accommodation Meals Local transportation Health insurance 8. Letter of Invitation From the Scientific Host The scientific host must provide a letter of invitation written in English . The letter must: Confirm that a place to work will be available during the proposed research period. Include a binding declaration from the host institution requesting the relevant research cost allowance. The host institution should therefore be involved in the preparation of the application rather than being contacted only after the application is submitted. Visit HERE to learn more about the AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grants 2026 How to Apply Applications must be submitted online using the application form provided by AGNES. The application form is: https://forms.gle/t57E7k9gTTtd7R7XA Applicants should carefully check their application before submitting it. The call specifically warns that applications that: Do not follow the stated guidelines; or Are missing required documents will be automatically rejected . Applicants should therefore make sure that all required documents are complete, correctly formatted, written in the required language, and included before submission. Application Language All applications must be submitted in English . This applies particularly to the research proposal, CV, scientific host invitation letter, and other documents where English is specifically required. Applicants whose academic transcripts use another language must provide the required official explanation of the grading system in English. Grant Acceptance and Reporting Requirements The grant is a once-off award and cannot be used to finance research stays retrospectively. If selected, both the grant recipient and the scientific host must provide: A signed letter of acceptance A contractual agreement These documents must be emailed to the AGNES Governing Board within two weeks of receiving the offer , according to the call information. Following completion of the research stay, both the grantee and scientific host are expected to report to AGNES on the progress and success of their collaboration. This report is expected within six months after completion of the research stay . Research Stay Timeline The selection meeting is scheduled for December 2026 . Only selected candidates will be notified. The earliest possible start date for research stays is: 1 March 2027 Research stays must be completed by: 31 July 2027 Applicants should therefore consider these dates when discussing the proposed research schedule with their scientific host. Important Dates Stage Date Application deadline 16 October 2026 at 23:59 GMT Selection meeting December 2026 Earliest research stay commencement 1 March 2027 Latest completion of research stay 31 July 2027 Key Points Applicants Should Understand Before applying, prospective applicants should pay particular attention to the following requirements: You must currently be registered for a doctoral degree. You must be a national of a sub-Saharan African country. You must have at least one thesis-related article published in an eligible journal. The journal must be indexed by SCOPUS or Web of Science. You must identify a scientific host in another sub-Saharan African country. Your host must agree to your proposal and work schedule. The proposed research must contribute to your doctoral research. The research must be relevant to development in sub-Saharan Africa. The research activity must not be possible in your home country. Your proposal must be written in English and must not exceed five pages. Your CV must use the AGNES template. You must provide academic transcripts. You must provide evidence of your eligible publications. You must provide two travel quotations. You must provide an estimated cost of living. You must provide a scientific host invitation letter. The complete application must be submitted online before the deadline. Missing documents or failure to follow the guidelines can result in automatic rejection. Why the Programme Matters The AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grant is structured around more than simply providing funding for a short research trip. The programme aims to strengthen research connections within Africa by allowing doctoral researchers to work with institutions and experienced researchers in other sub-Saharan African countries. This creates opportunities for researchers to gain access to expertise, facilities, research environments, and professional networks that may not be available at their home institutions. The programme also places emphasis on research that can contribute to the development of sub-Saharan African countries, meaning applicants are expected to demonstrate the wider relevance of their doctoral research. The involvement of scientific hosts also creates an opportunity for longer-term professional and research collaboration. Conclusion The AGNES Intra-Africa Mobility Grants for Junior Researchers 2026 provide doctoral researchers from sub-Saharan Africa with an opportunity to undertake a one- to two-month research stay at another African university or research institution. With grants of up to €3,000 , the programme can contribute toward travel, subsistence, and research-related costs while giving researchers an opportunity to collaborate with experienced scientists and strengthen their professional networks. The programme is open across academic disciplines, including Sciences, Humanities, Law, and Social Sciences , while the Special AGNES Mobility Grant provides an additional application route specifically for female researchers. However, applicants must meet several specific requirements, particularly being current doctoral students, having at least one eligible published thesis-related article, identifying a scientific host, and demonstrating that the proposed research cannot be conducted in their home country. Interested researchers should begin preparing their research proposal, publication evidence, host invitation, travel quotations, transcripts, and other required documents well before the deadline. title: Activate Fellowship 2027: $100,000 Annual Stipend and $100,000 R&D Support for Hard-Tech Founders
summary: Applications are now open for the Activate U.S. Fellowship Cohort 2027 , an opportunity designed for scientists, engineers, and technology professionals who are ready to move a promising hard-tech innovation from research and development toward commercialization. The Activate Fellowship is built specifically for technical founders developing hardware-based technologies in areas connected to the physical sciences, biological sciences, and related engineering disciplines. Rather than focusing only on business development, the fellowship provides financial support, entrepreneurship education, mentorship, professional development, community programming, and resources intended to help technical leaders build companies around transformative technologies. For the 2027 U.S. cohort, applications will close on October 30 at 12:00 p.m. Pacific Time . What Is the Activate Fellowship? The Activate Fellowship supports scientists, engineers, and technology leaders who are developing technologies with the potential to create significant real-world impact. The program is particularly focused on hard tech , meaning technologies that require substantial scientific, engineering, research, development, and commercialization work. Fellows are expected to have deep technical knowledge of the technology they are developing and to be capable of leading the technical work required to reduce the risks associated with bringing that technology to market. The fellowship is designed for people who are transitioning from technical expertise into company leadership and commercialization. This means applicants do not necessarily need to already be experienced entrepreneurs. In fact, Activate specifically states that fellows should be commercially developing a hardware-based technology for the first time and should not be repeat hard-tech founders. The program is intended to help bridge the gap between scientific or engineering innovation and the creation of commercially viable technologies. Activate Fellowship 2027 Benefits The fellowship provides substantial financial and professional support to selected fellows. 1. $100,000 Annual Living Stipend Fellows receive a $100,000 living stipend per year . This financial support is intended to help fellows dedicate themselves to their proposed project or company on a full-time basis. 2. $100,000 in R D Support The fellowship also provides $100,000 in research and development support . This is particularly important for hard-tech founders because developing physical technologies can require significant resources for experimentation, prototyping, testing, technical development, and other R D activities. 3. $12,000 for Travel and Professional Development Fellows receive $12,000 per year for travel and professional development . This can support activities that help fellows expand their technical and professional networks and continue developing their leadership and entrepreneurial capabilities. 4. Health Insurance Stipend The fellowship provides a health insurance stipend , adding another form of financial support for fellows as they dedicate themselves to their projects. 5. Relocation Allowance A relocation allowance is also included among the fellowship benefits. This can help fellows manage relocation-related expenses associated with participating in the program. Community and Collaboration The Activate Fellowship is not only a financial support program. Community participation is an important part of the fellowship experience. Fellows participate in community-based programming every two weeks , including: Workshops Fellow talks Networking opportunities Collaborative activities Professional development opportunities The program also facilitates what Activate describes as “Collisions” , which are opportunities for fellows to connect with inspiring people, expand their networks, and develop unexpected professional relationships. Activate emphasizes a community culture that prioritizes people and authentic relationships. The organization highlights principles such as putting people before the company and being genuine even when difficult situations arise. This community environment is intended to give fellows access to peers and experienced individuals who can provide perspectives, connections, and support throughout their entrepreneurial journey. Entrepreneurship Education and Support Scientists and engineers may have extensive technical expertise but limited experience with entrepreneurship, commercialization, company building, or business leadership. The Activate Fellowship provides education specifically designed to help address this transition. Elements of Entrepreneurship Fellows receive education tailored to the needs of the scientist-turned-founder . During the first quarter, fellows participate in a weekly Elements of Entrepreneurship course designed to help them develop the business and leadership knowledge needed to commercialize their technology. One-on-One Mentorship Fellows receive regular one-on-one mentorship with their community s Managing Director. These sessions can be used to work through challenges, evaluate strategies, and refine the direction of the company or proposed project. Quarterly Advisory Meetings The fellowship also provides quarterly advisory meetings that function similarly to board meetings . These meetings are intended to help fellows focus on the most important issues facing their companies and projects. Personal Development Activate also places emphasis on the individual fellow rather than focusing exclusively on the company. Annual retreats and reunions are designed to support fellows personal development and provide opportunities for continued connection within the Activate community. Who Is Eligible for the Activate Fellowship? Applicants must satisfy specific requirements relating to their education, technical experience, entrepreneurial stage, work authorization, and commitment to their proposed project. Bachelor s Degree Requirement Applicants must have a bachelor s degree . Scientific, Engineering, or Technology Experience Applicants must have at least four years of post-baccalaureate experience in: Scientific research Engineering Technology development This means the fellowship is intended for individuals who have already developed substantial technical experience beyond their undergraduate education. First-Time Hard-Tech Founder Applicants must be leading the commercial development of a hardware-based technology innovation for the first time if awarded the fellowship. In other words, the program is not designed for repeat hard-tech founders. The applicant should be moving toward commercializing a hard-tech innovation and taking on a leadership role in the proposed company or project. Full-Time Commitment Selected fellows must be prepared to commit full-time to their proposed project or company . Activate notes that applicants do not necessarily have to have already left their current job or incorporated their company when applying. The fellowship is designed in part to help enable that transition. U.S. Work Authorization Applicants must be legally able to work in the United States for the duration of the fellowship . This is an important requirement for applicants who are currently outside the United States or who do not currently have U.S. work authorization. English Communication Applicants must be able to communicate proficiently in English . This is important because fellows participate in entrepreneurship education, mentorship, community programming, networking, and other activities that require effective communication. Project Eligibility In addition to meeting the individual fellow requirements, the proposed technology must meet Activate s project eligibility requirements. Technology Must Be Based in Relevant Scientific or Engineering Fields The proposed project must be based in: Physical sciences Biological sciences Related engineering disciplines The program therefore focuses on technology that has a substantial scientific or engineering foundation. Technology Must Still Be in Development The project must still be in development at the application deadline. It must not yet be ready for full-scale product sales. This requirement reflects the fellowship s focus on helping technical innovations move through development and toward commercialization. Funding Limit At the time of the application deadline, the proposed project must not have raised more than $2 million in debt or equity funding from non-governmental sources . Applicants should therefore carefully consider the amount and type of funding their project has already received when determining eligibility. What Activate Looks For in Fellows Meeting the minimum eligibility requirements does not automatically mean that an applicant will be selected. Activate describes several characteristics it looks for when evaluating potential fellows. 1. Hard-Tech Leadership Activate wants applicants who can demonstrate leadership in developing transformative technologies. The ideal applicant should have a strong understanding of the technology they are proposing and be capable of independently leading the technical work involved. 2. Technical Expertise Applicants should have substantial technical knowledge in the field of their proposed project. They should be able to: Understand the technical challenges facing their technology Lead technical development Conduct or oversee research and development Reduce technical risks Explain complex technical concepts to non-technical audiences Activate notes that many successful applicants have completed PhDs or postdoctoral training. However, a PhD or postdoctoral background is not presented as an absolute requirement . Activate also welcomes people with technical or R D experience in industry or equivalent backgrounds. 3. Proof of Concept or Prototype Activate indicates that many successful applicants have already established an early proof of concept or prototype supported by experimental data demonstrating that their innovation works. This suggests that applicants should be able to provide evidence supporting the technical feasibility of their proposed innovation. The technology does not need to be ready for full-scale sales, but applicants should be able to demonstrate meaningful progress in development. 4. Transformative Potential Activate is interested in technologies that could make a significant difference in the world . The program looks beyond incremental improvements and asks applicants to consider the potential long-term impact of their technology. Applicants should be able to explain what the world could look like if their technology were successfully developed and implemented at scale. 5. Leadership Readiness Activate also looks for applicants who are ready to develop beyond their technical expertise and grow as business leaders. Applicants should demonstrate the ability or potential to: Lead a company Manage conflict Operate in uncertain situations Act with integrity Mobilize resources Make important decisions Work toward commercialization The applicant should have a leadership role in the proposed company or project. 6. High Potential Impact of the Fellowship Activate emphasizes additionality in its selection process. This means the organization wants to understand whether receiving the fellowship would meaningfully accelerate the applicant s professional development and the progress of their proposed project. Applicants should therefore be able to explain why the Activate Fellowship is important at this particular stage of their journey. A strong application should make clear how the fellowship s financial support, mentorship, education, community, and resources could change the trajectory of the technology and the applicant s development as a leader. Who Should Consider Applying? The Activate Fellowship may be relevant for technical professionals who are moving from research or engineering into commercialization. Potential applicants may include: Scientists developing a new technology Engineers working on hardware-based innovations Researchers transitioning toward entrepreneurship Technology developers with substantial R D experience Industry professionals developing a transformative technology Technical experts preparing to commercialize a prototype Scientists or engineers preparing to become first-time hard-tech founders Applicants should have a strong technical foundation and a project that fits Activate s hard-tech focus. APPLY HERE Application Process Applicants should follow the application instructions provided by Activate. The application page states that applicants should first click the “Apply for US Cohort 2027” button and complete the application interest form to receive the link to begin the application. Applicants should ensure that their proposed project clearly demonstrates: The scientific or engineering basis of the technology. The problem the technology is intended to address. The current development stage. Evidence that the technology works, where applicable. The potential impact of the technology. Their technical expertise and experience. Their leadership role in the project. Their plans for commercial development. Why the Activate Fellowship would significantly accelerate the project. Their ability to commit to the fellowship full-time if selected. Visit HERE to learn more about the Activate Fellowship 2027 Application Deadline Applications for the Activate U.S. Fellowship Cohort 2027 will close on: October 30 at 12:00 p.m. Pacific Time. Applicants should submit their application before the deadline rather than waiting until the final hours. Important Considerations Before Applying Before starting an application, prospective applicants should carefully assess both their own eligibility and the eligibility of their proposed technology. In particular, applicants should confirm that they: Have a bachelor s degree. Have at least four years of post-baccalaureate scientific research, engineering, or technology development experience. Are developing a hardware-based technology. Are commercializing the technology for the first time. Can commit full-time to the proposed project if selected. Are legally able to work in the United States for the duration of the fellowship. Can communicate proficiently in English. Have a project based in the physical sciences, biological sciences, or related engineering disciplines. Have not reached full-scale product sales. Have not raised more than $2 million in non-governmental debt or equity funding. Applicants should also consider whether they can clearly demonstrate the technical expertise, leadership potential, transformative impact, and development progress that Activate looks for in its fellows. Conclusion The Activate Fellowship 2027 is designed to help experienced scientists, engineers, and technology developers transition from technical innovation into hard-tech entrepreneurship and commercialization. Selected fellows receive significant financial support, including a $100,000 annual living stipend, $100,000 in R D support, $12,000 in annual travel and professional development funds, a health insurance stipend, and a relocation allowance . Beyond financial assistance, the program provides entrepreneurship education, mentorship, advisory support, community programming, networking, and personal development opportunities.
